title: Atomic task bundle transport
description: Adds one-file validated task submission, structured JSON task documents, automatic Airelay dispatch, and one-file results.

requirements.summary: Submit one complete atomic Git bus task
acceptance: AC-001: Protocol v2 discovers exactly one inbox taskbundle JSON file per task identity.
AC-002: The bundle contains one deterministic base64 tar.gz patch pack with exact digest, compressed size, uncompressed size, and entry count.
AC-003: Reusing a task ID with a different archive digest is rejected as task_id_content_changed.
AC-004: Bundle JSON is strict and duplicate keys, trailing data, unknown fields, invalid routing, and malformed timestamps are rejected.

AC-005: Archive extraction permits regular files only and rejects traversal, absolute or backslash paths, links, special files, duplicate paths, case-fold collisions, non-deterministic metadata, and size violations.
AC-006: AGENT_HANDOFF.md and manifest.json are mandatory and materialization uses a temporary directory followed by atomic rename.

requirements.summary: Use a structured JSON task document
acceptance: AC-007: task-spec.json and taskbundle.json use a validated task object with title, summary, objectives, constraints, acceptance criteria, and optional references.
AC-008: Protocol v2 materializes the task object as TASK_REQUEST.json instead of request.md.
AC-009: JSON is the only canonical gateway input; YAML is not parsed by the gateway and may only be converted externally before validation.
AC-010: Local task_execution_mode supports auto, manual, and disabled with auto as the default.
AC-011: Auto mode bypasses per-task approval and resumes stale waiting_for_approval state without owner intervention.
AC-012: Remote task data cannot select or weaken the local execution mode, repository path, Airelay session, or process policy.
AC-013: Explicit unresolved placeholder patterns remain rejected.
AC-014: Normal shell redirection, comparison operators, XML fragments, and angle brackets are accepted.
AC-015: AGENT_HANDOFF.md remains the only normative agent entry point and AGENT_RESPONSE.md remains the canonical response file.
AC-016: Protocol-v2 completion writes one results path containing state, archive digest, commits, gates, deviations, and human response.
AC-017: Intermediate execution states remain local and are not committed individually to the Git bus.
AC-018: Protocol-v1 directory tasks remain read-compatible for existing audit records.

requirements.summary: Build and validate bundles before publication
acceptance: AC-019: build-task-bundle.py resolves the exact planner commit pinned by manifest.workflow.commit and runs its semantic patch-pack validator.
AC-020: The builder creates a deterministic archive, independently validates the complete bundle, emits compact canonical JSON, and atomically renames the output.
AC-021: Invalid packs, unsafe archives, malformed task documents, checksum mismatches, and oversized one-file outputs fail without a final output file.

AC-022: Native Go and Python tests cover auto-mode recovery, canonical response recovery, deterministic bundles, immutable materialization, traversal, links, duplicate JSON keys, case-fold collisions, and structured task validation.
AC-023: No third-party Go or Python runtime dependency is introduced.
AC-024: Version and documentation advance to 0.2.0 and describe the protocol and security boundary.

gpt_static_checks_performed: Inspected gpt-review-planner main at 98f4b2848915857c64523fe9d5c67519ed621a2c and confirmed that validate-patch-pack.py, validate-patch-pack-delivery.py, patch manifest schema, and patch-pack handoff documentation already exist.
Identified that the current planner validator still requires AGENT_PROMPT.md and does not yet make patch-pack/AGENT_HANDOFF.md or protocol-v2 task bundles canonical.
Authored the complete gateway implementation, Go and Python tests, JSON schemas, documentation, builder, transport validator, and executable Git patch.
Parsed all Python sources and JSON artifacts, parsed all Go files, and performed source-level Go type checking without building or testing the project.
Applied the complete patch to a disposable content-equivalent clean repository and checked Git whitespace and exact file-operation scope.
gpt_runtime_checks_not_performed: go fmt ./... as an acceptance gate
live deterministic task-bundle publication to rceman/typer
installation, daemon restart, registry publication, and loopback readiness
local archive quarantine and Git bus housekeeping
known_integration_risks: The repository declares Go 1.24 and the local agent must use the configured Go 1.24 toolchain.
GitHub one-file publication through the Contents API is intentionally capped below one megabyte; larger future packs require a different blob transport rather than silently splitting one task.
Until the planner follow-up release is merged, bundles remain compatible with the pinned v1.2.0 validator by including AGENT_PROMPT.md in addition to canonical AGENT_HANDOFF.md.
The two failed bootstrap cleanup tasks must be archived from the bus before the updated daemon starts so they cannot dispatch concurrently into the same Airelay session.
forbidden_deviations: Do not move the canonical semantic patch-pack validator into rceman/typer or reimplement it as a divergent gateway contract.
Do not accept YAML directly in the gateway wire protocol or add a YAML dependency.
Do not restore per-task remote approval as the default trusted-bus execution model.
Do not weaken archive path, digest, size, regular-file-only, duplicate-key, duplicate-path, or task immutability checks.
Do not publish intermediate protocol-v2 statuses as separate Git commits.
Do not add third-party Go or Python dependencies, broaden repository file scope, or replace Airelay with direct Codex execution.
